peg: EPS is distorted by property depreciation.
forward_pe: P/FFO is the standard earnings multiple for REITs.

free_cash_flow_yield: Regulated utilities commonly fund large mandated capital programs.

peg: Point estimates are dominated by commodity-cycle assumptions.
operating_margin_trend: Trailing margin trend for a producer is the realized commodity price, not structural improvement.
incremental_margin: Incremental margin against a commodity-driven revenue denominator is cycle contamination; NEM published 128.2%.
fcf_growth_3y: Three-year FCF growth for a producer tracks the commodity cycle, not capital discipline.
gross_profits_to_assets: Gross profitability moves with realized price rather than asset productivity.

altman_z: Industrial distress scores do not represent pipeline and binary-event risk.

price_to_book: Book value does not capture pipeline probability.
free_cash_flow_yield: Cash burn should be evaluated as runway.
altman_z: Industrial distress scores do not represent clinical-stage solvency or binary-event risk.
return_on_invested_capital: Pre-profit biotechnology has no stable operating-return denominator.

capex_to_depreciation: A low capex-to-depreciation ratio is structural for a fabless designer that outsources fabrication, not evidence of under-investment. Distinguishing fabless from integrated manufacturers requires a filing parse this pipeline does not yet do, so the interpretation is suppressed for the whole industry rather than applied wrongly to part of it.
inventory_days_trend: Semiconductor inventory swings with the industry cycle and customer build plans; a rising trend is not an accounting-quality signal.

price_to_book: Insurance brokers earn commission and fee income and take no underwriting risk or investment float; acquisition-driven goodwill in this roll-up-heavy sub-industry makes book value uninformative -- valued like an asset-light services business, not an underwriter.
altman_z: Distress model calibrated for asset-heavy manufacturers; a fee-based broker carries no inventory or heavy fixed assets for it to read correctly.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Commission and fee income does not generate a receivable-days signal comparable to industrial DSO.

combined_ratio: Combined ratio is a P&C underwriting construct; medical loss ratio (health-plan costs over premium revenue) is the health-insurer analog.

forward_pe: Accelerated depreciation on an asset-intensive pipeline/storage base makes P/E nearly meaningless for midstream; EV/EBITDA is the sector-standard multiple.
peg: PEG compounds the same forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.
free_cash_flow_yield: Growth capex depresses FCF during the build phase; EV/EBITDA and distribution coverage (not yet computed by this pipeline) are the standard midstream reads, not FCF yield.
current_ratio: Midstream working capital is not the liquidity signal it is for an industrial company; leverage (net_debt_to_ebitda) and interest coverage carry that read instead.

forward_pe: Airlines are a textbook peak-earnings/trough-multiple cyclical; EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle margins is preferred to a point-in-time P/E, which reads cheapest exactly at the top of the cycle.
peg: PEG compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.
current_ratio: Airlines run structurally low current ratios by design -- advance ticket sales are a current liability that funds operations -- so this is not the liquidity signal it is for a typical industrial company.
Long-cycle program working capital (progress billings, customer advances) is not the short-term liquidity signal current ratio represents for a typical industrial company.
peg: Program-timing lumpiness in trailing growth breaks the PEG denominator; forward P/E against backlog-supported growth reads better.

gross_profits_to_assets: Capital-markets firms report no gross-profit line; trading and underwriting revenue over risk capital is the comparable read, approximated here by return on equity pending a computed net-revenue-per-risk-capital metric.

price_to_book: Asset managers are asset-light and fee-driven; earnings power (P/E) is the standard read, not balance-sheet book value.
net_debt_to_ebitda: Leverage is a minor input to an asset-light, fee-revenue business model.
current_ratio: Working-capital liquidity is not the balance-sheet risk that matters here; AUM, net flows, and fee-rate stability are (not yet computed by this pipeline beyond the unaudited filing-extraction layer).
gross_profits_to_assets: No meaningful gross-profit-to-assets frame for a fee-based, asset-light business.

altman_z: Heavy land and work-in-process inventory carrying, plus structurally elevated leverage through the build cycle, break the industrial-manufacturer calibration Altman's model assumes.
free_cash_flow_yield: Cash flow moves inversely to growth for a homebuilder: land and work-in-process spend consumes cash fastest exactly when order growth (and future revenue) is strongest, so FCF yield reads worst at the best points in the cycle.
ev_to_fcf: Same cash-flow-inverted-to-growth distortion as free_cash_flow_yield above.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Homebuilder receivables are not a meaningful earnings-quality signal set against work-in-process inventory accounting.
accruals_ratio: Land and work-in-process inventory accounting produces structurally large accruals unrelated to the earnings-quality signal this ratio targets elsewhere.

forward_pe: Merchant power prices are commodity-cyclical; a point-in-time P/E is the same peak-earnings/trough-multiple trap it is for other commodity producers.
peg: PEG compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion, on the same grounds as forward_pe above.

forward_pe: Capital-goods order books are peak-earnings/trough-multiple cyclical, the same pattern as airline.
peg: Compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion as forward_pe above.
capex_to_depreciation: Depreciation base lags for OEMs that outsource fabrication; capex/revenue is the comparable reinvestment read.
inventory_days_trend: Long production/backlog cycles make inventory swing with order books, not accounting quality, the same reasoning as semiconductor.

forward_pe: Electrification-driven demand makes trailing growth unusually lumpy; same cyclical logic as machinery.
peg: Compounds the same cyclical forward-P/E distortion.
capex_to_depreciation: Depreciation base lags for equipment makers that outsource fabrication; capex/revenue is the comparable read.
inventory_days_trend: Inventory swings with order books, not accounting quality, the same reasoning as semiconductor/machinery.

free_cash_flow_yield: Kiln/quarry capex consumes cash fastest exactly when volume growth is strongest, the same cash-inverted-to-growth logic as homebuilder.
capex_to_depreciation: Quarry/plant capital intensity reads better against revenue than a depreciation base that varies with asset age.

current_ratio: Progress billings and customer advances distort short-term liquidity, identical to aerospace_defense.
peg: Program-timing lumpiness breaks the PEG denominator, same as aerospace_defense.
accruals_ratio: Percentage-of-completion accounting produces structurally large accruals unrelated to earnings quality, same logic as homebuilder.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Unbilled receivables swing with project mix, not collection quality.

free_cash_flow_yield: Mandated network-maintenance and PTC capex programs, the same rationale as utility.
capex_to_depreciation: Rail's core efficiency KPI is operating ratio, not a depreciation-relative capex read; capex_intensity is tracked alongside as a replacement metric.
inventory_days_trend: Minimal fuel/parts inventory carries no meaningful signal.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Freight billing aging is not a meaningful quality-of-earnings signal for a railroad.

operating_margin_trend: Year-over-year margin swings mechanically with fuel-surcharge pass-through revenue, a low-margin dollar-for-dollar reimbursement that dilutes the ratio without reflecting real efficiency change.
forward_pe: Truckload spot-rate freight cycle is peak-earnings/trough-multiple, the same pattern as airline.
capex_to_depreciation: Distinguishes asset-based carriers from asset-light brokers sharing the same industry tag.
inventory_days_trend: No meaningful inventory for a trucking carrier.

capex_to_depreciation: Discriminates integrated parcel/air networks (high capex) from asset-light forwarders (low capex) sharing one industry tag.
inventory_days_trend: No meaningful inventory for a logistics-services business.

peg: Charter-rate cycles dominate point estimates exactly like a commodity producer; reuses that profile's own replacement target.
operating_margin_trend: Trailing margin trend mostly reflects the period's realized charter rate, not structural efficiency, mirroring commodity_producer.
capex_to_depreciation: Vessel newbuild/drydock capex is lumpy and age-dependent; capex/revenue is the more comparable fleet-investment read.

free_cash_flow_yield: Recurring landfill-cell development and fleet capex is structurally heavy, the same mandated-capex logic as utility.
capex_to_depreciation: Landfill/fleet reinvestment reads better against revenue scale than a depreciation base.

price_to_book: Roll-up M&A goodwill and minimal tangible book, identical reasoning to insurance_broker.
altman_z: Distress model calibrated for asset-heavy manufacturers, same as insurance_broker.
capex_to_depreciation: Near-zero PP&E base makes the ratio noisy; ROIC/FCF-yield is the real read for an asset-light, people-based business.

price_to_book: Roll-up M&A goodwill and minimal tangible book, identical reasoning to insurance_broker/staffing.
altman_z: Distress model calibrated for asset-heavy manufacturers, same as staffing.
capex_to_depreciation: Near-zero PP&E base makes the ratio noisy for an asset-light, people-based business.
Directionally reasonable reinvestment read, though most names in this tag run similarly low and it is the least discriminating of the industrials group for that reason.

peg: Patent-cliff step-downs make trailing-growth-based PEG denominators as unstable as program-timing lumpiness is for aerospace & defense.
revenue_growth: Trailing growth nets a compounding base business against a specific product's loss-of-exclusivity step-down into a number describing neither; consensus targets already price known patent expirations.
earnings_growth: Same loss-of-exclusivity step-down distortion on the EPS side.
fcf_growth_3y: Three-year FCF growth swings with the same loss-of-exclusivity step-down, not capital discipline.

inventory_days_trend: Consignment/loaner-unit inventory held at hospital sites inflates inventory-days independent of demand -- a structural placement-model effect, not an accounting-quality signal.
peg: Single-product FDA-approval/launch timing makes trailing growth lumpy, the same mechanism as aerospace & defense's program-timing rule.
days_sales_outstanding_trend: Hospital/GPO contract terms and large capital-equipment placement deals with extended payment terms make DSO swings a deal-mix artifact, not a collections signal.

gross_profits_to_assets: This sub-industry is a serial-acquirer roll-up model, so accumulated goodwill inflates the assets denominator and depresses GP/assets regardless of underlying instrument/reagent profitability, the same goodwill argument as insurance_broker.
peg: Revenue here is tied to the external biotech-funding cycle, not company execution, breaking PEG the same way a commodity cycle breaks it for commodity_producer.
revenue_growth: Trailing growth measures the biotech industry's capital-raising cycle more than management execution.

gross_profits_to_assets: Passthrough wholesale revenue produces a structurally near-zero gross margin by design, which this factor reads as maximal unprofitability rather than competitive weakness.
incremental_margin: On a ~3% gross margin base, single-basis-point mix shifts move incremental margin by huge relative swings unrelated to real operating leverage.
profit_margin: Distribution economics convert thin per-unit margin into acceptable returns via massive asset turnover; a flat margin band penalizes the business model itself, while ROIC already captures the turnover-adjusted return.

peg: Long implementation/sales cycles and heavy stock compensation routinely produce negative or noisy trailing EPS growth in scale-up, breaking PEG the same way it is assumed to break generically for other_pre_profit, but for a recurring-revenue reason specific to this profile.
altman_z: Asset-light, recurring-revenue business carries no meaningful inventory/working-capital profile for the distress model to read, the same argument as asset_manager.
inventory_days_trend: No inventory, same precedent as asset_manager/insurance_broker.
capex_to_depreciation: Reinvestment here is R&D/S&M-driven, not capex; a low ratio would misleadingly read as underinvestment the same way it does for a fabless semiconductor designer, and stock-comp intensity is the truer reinvestment signal.

price_to_book: Water utilities trade at a persistent premium reflecting scarcity of water rights and ESG-driven capital inflows, not balance-sheet mispricing; absolute price-to-book bands calibrated on the broader utility set would misread every water name as overvalued.
capex_to_depreciation: Multi-decade lead/aging-pipe replacement cycles run this ratio structurally high, the inverse of the fabless-semiconductor problem but the same structural-not-anomalous argument.

peg: Tax-equity/HLBV accounting noise in reported EPS breaks PEG, the same cyclical-forward-P/E trap noted for independent_power_producer/commodity_producer but driven by accounting structure rather than commodity price.
forward_pe: GAAP EPS for a yieldco is structurally distorted by accelerated depreciation and non-cash tax-equity allocations; EV/EBITDA on contracted cash flow is the sector-standard read, the same logic as midstream_mlp.
free_cash_flow_yield: Reported FCF is depressed during the growth/build phase by construction financing draws, not owner-distributable cash.
net_debt_to_ebitda: Project-level non-recourse debt against contracted assets reads very differently from corporate leverage; a blended net-debt/EBITDA overstates risk versus a diversified operating company.

_comment: Two rules per metric per business profile. APPLICABILITY: `rules` declares whether a metric is meaningful for a profile at all (suppressed/replaced/applied). REQUIRED_FOR_SCORE: `required_for_score` declares which metrics a parent factor cannot publish without. Both are read by the LIVE scorer (pipeline/scorer.py) as well as the v2 layer -- previously only the v2 shadow path consulted this file, so the correct insurer rules below existed and governed nothing a user saw. See research/audit/CURRENT_MODEL_AUDIT.md section 5.

required_for_score._comment: category -> metrics the category score cannot be published without. A missing required metric makes the parent category null rather than quietly renormalizing onto whatever else resolved. Publishing a Value score of 96 for an insurer whose price-to-book was never scored is the failure this prevents.
